summary: HTTP/2 connection pool reuse blocked by egress ACL causing FIN/ACK drop and TLS session reuse leading to corrupted range downloads in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Customer NovaBI reports intermittent corruption of model shard range downloads from Redwood artifact storage in their private deployment. Corruption manifests as either checksum mismatch on concatenated ranges or truncated shard files leading to model load errors. Impact: Serving nodes drop to degraded capacity for affected model; endpoints return 5xx or stall during large-generation requests. Users see increased latency and token errors.

Observed behaviour: Failure occurs only in private deployment behind customer-managed egress ACL and corporate proxy appliance. Failures correlate with heavy concurrent range downloads and long-lived HTTP/2 multiplexed connections. Network traces show missing FIN/ACK frames from server->client path leading to connection pool reuse with stale TLS session context, which then causes range requests to be served on a re-used TCP stream with partial TLS state mismatch and corrupted byte ranges.

Expected behaviour: Normal HTTP/2 connection pool reuse should only occur when connections are cleanly closed; FIN/ACK suppression at the egress should not result in TLS session reuse that corrupts presigned range downloads.

Customer impact: Production model serve regressions for multiple product teams at NovaBI; estimated 12% of large shard downloads affected during peak ingestion windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private Redwood control plane with NovaBI egress ACL + corporate proxy enabled
2) Trigger parallel model shard range downloads by starting 24 concurrent model containers requesting 4-8 range slices each
3) Observe artifact fetch logs on serving nodes and client-side checksum validation failures
4) Capture packet trace at customer egress appliance and on serving node to compare TCP FIN/ACK visibility
5) Correlate timestamps with Redwood artifact service access logs to identify partial byte ranges returned
logs: serving-node/artifact-fetcher INFO 2026-03-12T08:12:33Z: presigned-fetch range 0-1048575 started (req id: req-6b9d)
serving-node/artifact-fetcher WARN 2026-03-12T08:12:34Z: range 1/4 checksum mismatch after concatenation, expected sha256:aa3f.. got: aa2c.. (req id: req-6b9d)
envoy-proxy WARN 2026-03-12T08:12:35Z: http2 stream reset by remote, no RST frame seen from upstream
tcpdump: 08:12:34.123 IP 10.2.1.8.443 > 172.31.10.5.51094: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12567 ack 9876 win 64240 (payload),  -- FIN/ACK from server expected at 08:12:36 but not observed on egress side
artifact-storage access-log 2026-03-12T08:12:34Z: GET /models/gptx-large-v1/shard-12?range=0-1048575 206 Partial Content 200ms req-6b9d
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12: Initial triage by support: pattern matches FIN suppression or stateful firewall dropping FINs on post-connection tail packets
Packet captures show the server sent a FIN but the customer egress capture does not show the FIN leaving the customer appliance consistently
Envoy histograms show elevated http2 stream reset counts during peak concurrent downloads

Hypothesis: Egress ACL or inline proxy performs TCP stream rewriting or connection pooling that suppresses FIN to keep connections alive, causing upstream server to think connection closed while downstream client reuses connection with stale TLS record state
Reproduction attempt in Redwood staging without customer egress appliance failed — indicates issue is customer-e2e network dependent
SRE note: gRPC keepalive settings are standard; serving runtime relies on clean TCP close before reusing connection for next TLS session to the same destination when presigned URL reusage occurs
comments: Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Received initial report from NovaBI engineering. Requested packet captures at both customer egress and serving node. Asked customer to run tcpdump for 5 minutes during a heavy ingest window.
NovaBI-Eng (customer) 2026-03-12: Uploaded captures and flow logs to secure bucket. Observed that their NGFW shows 'connection persist' rules with 'no-fin' enabled for HTTP/2 to reduce churn.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-13: Confirmed missing FIN in customer egress capture. Temporarily asked customer to disable 'no-fin' behavior on NGFW or create an exception for artifact storage IPs. Provided test ACL to allow FIN/ACK propagation.

NovaBI-Eng 2026-03-13: Temporarily adjusted NGFW rule as requested; reported immediate drop in corrupted downloads during afternoon window. Will schedule a wider rollback test tomorrow morning when load is higher.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-14: Proposed long-term mitigation: instrument serving runtime to detect reused connection with unexpected TLS sequence and force fresh connection handshake for presigned range requests. Logged feature ticket INT-45012 for implementation and added tests to artifact-fetcher to validate correct FIN handling semantics.
Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-14: Notified customer that temporary mitigation is in place and that Redwood SRE will track implementation of permanent fix. SLA updated to P1 follow-up cadence.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: NovaBI disabled NGFW 'no-fin/connection persist' rule for artifact storage endpoints and corruption rate dropped to baseline. Long-term fix: serving runtime will be updated to detect stale connection TLS state and proactively perform connection reset before reusing streams for presigned range concatenation (tracking INT-45012). Follow-up: customer to roll out controlled test tomorrow; SRE to validate with synthetic large-range workload and update runbook.
next_steps: 1) Customer to run high-concurrency regression test with NGFW exception active and upload capture for validation (owner: NovaBI, due: 2026-03-15)
2) SRE to implement connection-state check and safe-reset for artifact-fetcher (owner: Liam O'Connor, ticket INT-45012)
3) Add anomaly alert to Console for increased http2 reset ratio and checksum failures on presigned downloads (owner: Platform Observability)
4) Update private-deploy runbook with NGFW configuration guidance and include a troubleshooting checklist for FIN/ACK suppression scenarios (owner: Docs)
